verdicts.reason: A: the CTA is a tiny pill crammed into the top-right corner and loses all prominence. 'Ships late June' is squeezed into a narrow column and breaks over three lines. The 'LIMITED SUMMER RELEASE' eyebrow sits orphaned under the logo panel instead of above the headline. The legal text is about as large as the body copy and sits right against the CTA, so the right half is a cramped jumble. B: the reading order works (logo panel, then eyebrow, headline and divider, then body, then a large CTA with 'Ships late June' underneath), and the CTA stands out properly. Its flaws: the headline is small for the space, the body copy and legal text are jammed into one stack with almost no gap and end in an orphan word ('solstice.'), and the legal text is too small to read at this size.
